title: Pet-Friendly Hotels in St. Louis, Missouri | PetTripFinder
meta_description: Verified pet-friendly hotels across downtown St. Louis, the Central West End, Clayton, Lambert airport and North County, Westport, Chesterfield and West County, St. Charles, and the Illinois Metro East, with real pet fees and policies read from each hotel's own official website.
introductory_copy: Every listing links to a pet policy verified directly from the hotel's own official website.
_boundary_note: PTF-ST-LOUIS-MARKET-001 Greater St. Louis bi-state traveler market, not the St. Louis MO-IL MSA and not a county line. INCLUDED: the City of St. Louis; all of St. Louis County; northern Jefferson County to Arnold and Imperial; the developed eastern two-thirds of St. Charles County out to Wentzville and Foristell; the Eureka-Pacific I-44 shoulder; and the Illinois Metro East lodging belt -- Madison County (Collinsville, Edwardsville, Glen Carbon, Granite City, Pontoon Beach, Maryville, Troy, Hamel, Alton, Godfrey, Bethalto, Wood River, East Alton), St. Clair County (Fairview Heights, Caseyville, East St. Louis, Sauget, Cahokia Heights, Belleville, Swansea, Shiloh, O'Fallon IL, Mascoutah/Scott AFB) and the contiguous Monroe County city of Columbia. EXCLUDED as deliberate boundary decisions, each recorded in the census candidate ledger with its reason and its discovered lodging: Waterloo IL (62298, Monroe County, three properties -- 25 road miles south and its own small market); Pevely and House Springs (63070, 63051, southern Jefferson County); Festus and Crystal City; St. Clair MO and Union MO (63077, Franklin County, I-44 beyond Pacific); New Melle (63073); Wright City (63390, Warren County); Hillsboro; and Ste. Genevieve. Every one of those markets itself with St. Louis language and none of them is a place a St. Louis traveller stays. Corridor assignment is by five-digit postal code throughout, with city/state as the fallback tier: the mailing city 'St. Louis' spans thirty ZIPs across four counties and eight distinct traveller areas, so a city-first assignment would put an airport hotel downtown.
